MeshSync Privacy Policy

Effective date: 1 November 2026

MeshSync is a file-synchronisation app for Android, made by Reino Eterno. It is available on Google Play and the Amazon Appstore. This policy explains what happens to your information when you use it.

The short version: MeshSync has no ads, no analytics, no tracking and no accounts. We run no servers and receive none of your data. Your files go directly between your own devices, encrypted.

How MeshSync works

MeshSync is a user interface for Syncthing, an open-source file-synchronisation engine. The Syncthing engine is built into the app and runs on your device. Folders you choose are synchronised with other devices that you explicitly approve, and only with them. The developer of MeshSync is not a party to that exchange and has no access to it.

What the app stores on your device

  • Synchronised folders and their files, in the places you choose on your device’s storage;
  • Syncthing’s configuration and index — your device name and its cryptographic device ID and certificate, the list of folders and of approved devices (their names and IDs), and a database describing the files being synchronised;
  • a local API key and port that the app generates so that it can talk to the engine. They are only reachable from your own device (127.0.0.1);
  • app preferences — theme, language, automatic acceptance of folder offers, and whether you finished the introduction;
  • conflict backups — when a sync conflict is resolved, the replaced version is moved to a .stversions/ folder inside the synchronised folder instead of being deleted.

Uninstalling the app removes its configuration and database. Synchronised files stay where they are on your device storage until you delete them. The app turns off Android’s automatic backup, so this data is not copied to your Google account backup by the app.

What goes over the network

When you connect devices, the Syncthing engine communicates over the internet or your local network:

  • File contents and metadata are exchanged only with the devices you have approved. Connections are encrypted with TLS and each device is verified by its device ID.
  • Local discovery — the engine announces itself on your local network (using multicast, hence the Wi-Fi multicast permission) so your own devices can find each other.
  • Global discovery — by default, Syncthing publishes your device ID and current network addresses to, and queries them from, public discovery servers run by the Syncthing project, so devices can find each other across networks. This sends your device ID and IP address, but no file names or contents.
  • Relays — when two devices cannot connect directly, Syncthing may use public relay servers run by volunteers. Relays only forward encrypted traffic and cannot read it, but they can see the devices’ IP addresses and the connection’s size and timing.
  • Your IP address is visible to the devices you sync with and to the discovery and relay servers above, as with any internet connection.

These services belong to the Syncthing community, not to us, and are subject to their own practices (see syncthing.net). The app does not send Syncthing usage reports, and automatic engine upgrades are disabled.

No ads, no analytics, no tracking

  • There is no advertising, and no advertising ID is used.
  • There are no analytics, crash-reporting, attribution or tracking tools, and no third-party SDKs that collect data.
  • We do not sell, rent or trade any information, and we do not profile you.
  • There are no accounts, in-app purchases or subscriptions.

Permissions

On Android, MeshSync asks for:

  • Internet, network state and Wi-Fi state — to synchronise with your other devices;
  • Wi-Fi multicast — for local discovery on your network;
  • All files access (Android 11+) and storage read/write (older versions) — because your synchronised folders live in shared storage, outside the app’s private area. The app reads and writes only the folders you add and does not browse anything else;
  • Notifications and foreground service — a persistent notification keeps the synchronisation running while the app is closed, and shows its status;
  • Camera — only when you choose to scan a device’s QR code. The image is processed on the device and is never stored or sent.

The app does not access your contacts, location, microphone or messages.

How long we keep things

We keep nothing, because we receive nothing. Data on your devices stays until you delete it or uninstall the app. Data held by the Syncthing discovery and relay services is subject to those services’ own retention.

Deleting your data

Remove a device or folder in the app to stop sharing it, delete the files on your devices if you no longer want them, and uninstall the app to remove its configuration. To remove your device ID from the public discovery servers, stop the app; entries expire on their own shortly afterwards. Because we hold no data about you, there is nothing for us to delete on our side.

Your rights

Depending on where you live (for example under the LGPD in Brazil, or the GDPR in the European Economic Area and the United Kingdom), you may have rights to access, correct or delete your data and to object to its use. Since we neither collect nor store personal data, those rights are exercised directly on your own devices. If you have any question, write to the address below and we will answer within 30 days.

Children

MeshSync is a general-purpose utility and is not directed at children. We do not knowingly collect any information from anyone, children included.

Changes to this policy

If this policy changes, the new version will be published at this same address with a new effective date. Significant changes will also be mentioned in the app’s release notes.

Contact

Questions about this policy: Adam Foerster, contact@meshsync.reinoeterno.online.
